text: 我感覺林大廚也是沒有惡意啦，就是作為廚師的想法，菜品放太久 怕顧客嚐的口感就會沒那麼好，特別是有點實力的廚師對自己的出品會更加有嚴格要求，而且還是在法國米其林餐廳裏推薦中餐給法國人，肯定想做到最好，別砸了招牌。 而且出餐口也都放滿了，感覺出了一段時間大廚才開始急的，看他開始有說是想叫一天叫外面的人出餐，但沒有人有空怕忙不過來，所以才想叫一天幫忙出餐的。 不過在片段中林大廚像一直黑面也感覺態度不太好，但也有可能是節目組特意剪輯出來，畢竟廚師在認真做菜沒有什麼表情也正常。 起碼胡一天情緒很穩定，也有一直安撫林，沒有太多爭執，最後互相也有給台階下啦🤗

text: This is exactly how it is. Ive studied for 15+ years. In the beginning , it’s always “your Chinese is so good!”. Then, when I could really start having complex conversations with Chinese folk, they were picking me apart left and right! Sometimes I got tired of getting corrected so much! 😂 all is good now though, now they just treat me like they’re talking to another Chinese person.

video_title: Your Chinese Is So Good | Des Bishop
text:
Every language has a different attitude to foreigners learning their language! Mandarin speakers will be surprised and supportive, but be brutally honest to correct you. Dutch speakers will question your sanity as to why you will even bother to learn Dutch, "Ben je gek? Het is toch niet nodig??" Irish speakers will LOVE anyone with even a couple of Irish words "cúpla focail" but feel immensely guilty that they can't speak Irish as well as they should be able to. German speakers will nod politely and then correct your grammar as precisely and bluntly as possible. And maybe switch to English. French speakers will just say "quoi?" with an annoyed tone and refuse to even think you're speaking the same language as them. English speakers will just assume you speak their specific dialect and accent and will make zero effort to accommodate to you, because well, everyone speaks English and nobody cares how well you speak it, really. And then if you speak Tamil, Kannada or other Indian languages other than Hindi, you will be invited into somebody home and offered a bed, amazing food and a friend for life.

But thats just what I've experienced as someone interested in languages!

@Velvetec  What even is a deep take? Like this take is all about a foreigner experience in China, and it is an accurate depiction. But getting past that first time in China, staying for longer, would yield more details about Chinese society.

A deeper take would be about how regional locals all talk poorly about other regional cuisines, touting their own as the best food. Like someone from the north would say that noodles and bread products made from flour and oats are the best and that southern food is too oily and greasy. Then someone from the south would complain at how dry and unpalatable food from the north is, citing rice as superior, with dishes being “rice-shoveling dishes” as the best, because the heavy flavor and spiciness would go well with white rice. The amount of disdain there is for other regions’ food is absurd, but there is often very little distinction made in a country like the USA, where it’s all labeled Chinese food, when I actuality there are 8 great regional cuisines in different areas of China based on agricultural availability.

Another deep take would be how learning Mandarin Chinese can’t really get you all too much in terms of personal rapport. If you go anywhere in China, there’s Mandarin Chinese that is universally spoken, but mostly in transactional and formal settings. The real way to get close with locals is to learn the local dialect, which is often kinda like mandarin, but someone from the southwest would likely have a difficult time understanding someone from the northeast of China. 

A deep take would be delving into details of friction caused by regional diversity of food or dialect, for one. Like how a polite word in one area may be mistaken for a dirty curse in another area. 

An observation about the widespread usage of digital currency, to the point where cash is so rarely seen and some kids may not recognize certain bills (not unlike USA with $2 bills).

​ @valtsarsky  не стоит делать такие однозначные заявления как "невозможно прочитать", не зная как функционируют китайские иероглифы. Большинство китайских иероглифов состоят из двух частей: смысловой и фонетической, т.е. одна часть указывает на категорию, вторая на то, как иероглиф произносится. Если вам встречается незнакомый иероглиф такого рода, его примерное произношение можно угадать с помощью фонетического компонента, а значение — из контекста и смысловой половинки.
Несколько примеров:
丁 произносится как dīng; добавили крышу и вход, получился 亭 — павильон (звучит как tíng), слева человек, получится 停 — пауза/перерыв (тоже tíng), слева добавили женщину, получился 婷 — "грациозная" (произношение снова tíng) и т.д.
